t:
The following sections of title 37, United States Code, are amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”:
    (1) Section 312(f), relating to special pay for nuclear-qualified officers extending period of active service. 
    (2) Section 312b(c), relating to nuclear career accession bonus. 
    (3) Section 312c(d), relating to nuclear career annual incentive bonus.

fable.w: This section only extends expiration dates for special pay and bonus authorities for nuclear-qualified military officers. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. There is no real tempting opposite reading; the text is a pure date amendment.
fable.s: are amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”

opus.w: This section only extends the expiration dates for special pays and bonuses for nuclear-qualified military officers. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. The bonuses are benefits, and benefits don't count as participation.
opus.s: The following sections of title 37, United States Code, are amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”
opus.b: **Step 1, thinking it through:** One might be tempted by the words "nuclear career accession bonus", since an accession bonus is a benefit that people apply for. But applying for a benefit doesn't count as participation under the definition. The section only pushes back expiration dates for military special pays. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and there's no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that extends the expiration date for certain military pay and bonus provisions. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The change is made directly by statute without requiring input from the officers, states, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: The following sections of title 37, United States Code, are amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that extending the period for bonuses involves some form of consultation or participation with the officers receiving them. However, the text is purely a technical amendment to statutory dates. It does not mention any process for consulting with officers, states, or the public. It is a unilateral legislative change to eligibility periods.
